meta.title: Emerson's cure for living someone else's life

plates.query: portrait of Ralph Waldo Emerson 19th century
Caspar David Friedrich lone figure on a mountain peak
Frederic Edwin Church sunrise wilderness landscape painting

beats.text: Emerson noticed how quickly we hand our lives over to the opinions of the crowd.
We dress, speak, and even think to win a nod from people we barely respect.
His remedy was two words: "Trust thyself." Every heart, he said, vibrates to that iron string.
The thought you dismiss as merely your own is exactly the one the world is waiting to hear.
"Whoso would be a man," he wrote, "must be a nonconformist."
Yes, you'll be misunderstood. So were Socrates, Galileo, every mind that ever moved us forward.
Imitation is suicide. Envy is ignorance. The one life that is yours to live is your own.
